newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia non-CIS wheat imports seen rising.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia non-CIS wheat imports seen rising.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent reasearch organistion specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA MAY INCREASE NON-CIS WHEAT IMPORTS IN EARLY SPRING

Russian wheat-consuming regions, particularly in the European part of the country, may increase wheat imports over the next two months despite a rise in production. This assumes a normal rate of consumption.

Farm wheat stocks remain very tight nearly at last year's reduced level. Despite the increased output, a significant part of the 1996 harvest was estimated to be of low quality and could be used only for feed.
It particularly concerns the North Caucasus and Povolzhsk regions, where only 38 pct and 52 pct of total wheat production respectively can be used for bread making.

In July-December 1996, Russian wheat and flour imports fell by 35 percent and 59 percent respectively on the same period of 1995. There are three main reasons accounting for the decline in the Russian imports --
- Some recovery in Russia's wheat production which increased to 34.9 million tonnes last year, compared with 30.1 million tonnes in 1995.

- A serious decline in wheat output affected Ukraine and Hungary which were the Russian major wheat suppliers in 1995/96 after Kazakhstan. In addition, a 10-percent value added tax imposed last September on food processed products imported from Ukraine to Russia has seriously cut competitiveness of the Ukrainian wheat flour at the Russian market.
- Financial constraints continue limiting effective demand of the Russian potential buyers.
